components.title: Midwest diesel rises 5.1% in a week
components.summary: EIA’s 14 September Midwest diesel benchmark is $6.250/gal, up $0.304 from $5.946. Watershed’s actual surcharge exposure is unknown.
components.factorRationale: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
components.causalPath: Retail diesel ↑ → carrier fuel surcharges → delivered costs. Exposure 75 assumes truck reliance; severity 70 reflects a 5.1% weekly move. Confidence 70, persistence 70, velocity 80, dependency 80 and substitutability 35 are provisional analyst judgments.
components.verify: Freight contracts, surcharge lag, outbound miles and customer pass-through.
components.action: Ask logistics and finance to quantify surcharge sensitivity for the next shipping cycle.
components.trigger: Another >5% weekly rise or contracted transport costs >5% above plan.

components.title: Grain outlook tightens; specialty basis still unknown
components.summary: September WASDE projects U.S. total-grain ending stocks of 62.92 Mt versus 65.03 Mt in August. That is a broad context signal, not a popcorn forecast.
components.factorRationale: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
components.causalPath: Broad grain balance → potential feed/grain pricing → formula costs. All seven factors are uncalibrated proxies (45/55/45/80/45/55/60); popping-grade corn and food-grade contracts can diverge materially.
components.verify: Actual grains, specification basis, origin, contracts and inventory cover.
components.action: Track supplier quotations before changing coverage or formulations.
components.trigger: Two relevant supplier quotes worsen >10%, or verified cover falls below the approved operating threshold.

components.title: Traceability planning requires a product-form decision
components.summary: FDA describes a proposed extension and a congressional direction not to enforce the rule before 20 July 2028. Applicability still depends on covered food and form.
components.factorRationale: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
components.causalPath: Covered receiving/transformation → KDE/CTE obligations → systems and partner coordination. Scope is not established for Watershed; factors 55/65/65/90/25/70/60 reflect planning exposure rather than a violation.
components.verify: Food Traceability List applicability at each process stage; exemptions; customer contractual dates.
components.action: Quality and IT should map covered inputs and data exchanges, retaining product-specific legal review.
components.trigger: Final regulatory change, customer deadline, or a confirmed gap in an applicable traceability process.

components.title: Pet formats offer a qualified commercial opening
components.summary: APPA projects $69.7bn of pet-food and treat sales for 2026. This does not establish unit growth or freeze-dried segment growth.
components.factorRationale: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
components.causalPath: Pet-category spending → candidate launch budgets → topper/inclusion projects suited to advertised capabilities. Factors 70/60/45/85/45/65/65 reflect an unvalidated sales hypothesis, not Watershed revenue.
components.verify: Premium segment units, brand launch plans, current capacity and qualified process fit.
components.action: Build a small list of qualified topper/inclusion prospects and test demand before reserving capacity.
components.trigger: Documented customer briefs and trial conversion, with confirmed available capacity and validated safety controls.
components.dateNote: APPA projection publication date unverified; baseline evidence, not a new event on retrieval day.

components.title: Popcorn expansion is an opportunity to verify
components.summary: Deer Creek’s public directory now lists Aunt Em’s / Heartland together. The reported equipment transition remains unverified as completed.
components.factorRationale: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
components.causalPath: Announced process additions → possible new formats → private-label prospects. Factors 70/65/60/85/40/75/60 assume qualification work; no incremental capacity is counted as operational.
components.verify: Equipment ownership, commissioning, production qualification and available slots.
components.action: Confirm the production milestone before offering new formats or delivery commitments.
components.trigger: Verified commissioned capacity plus a qualified customer opportunity.

components.title: Baby-food lead guidance has a material scope exclusion
components.summary: The FDA final guidance excludes grain-based and freeze-dried snacks. It must not be applied automatically to every toddler product.
components.factorRationale: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
components.causalPath: SKU classification → applicable contaminant requirements/customer specifications → testing and release criteria. Low velocity 20 reflects an existing rule, not new contamination. Other factors are analytical prioritization.
components.verify: Each SKU’s form, age positioning, state rules and customer specifications.
components.action: Keep contaminant controls; have Quality document the correct guidance scope by SKU.
components.trigger: Changed FDA/state requirements or an actual out-of-spec result; then use the approved food-safety response process.

components.title: Central Illinois storm outlook reaches three facility counties
components.summary: NWS includes McLean, Woodford and Tazewell counties in today’s thunderstorm/heavy-rain outlook, with localized flooding possible and some severe-storm potential Saturday. No facility disruption is established.
components.factorRationale: Exposure 85 reflects matched public locations, not confirmed damage; severity 55 assumes potentially manageable access/delivery interruption; confidence 80 reflects the primary regional outlook with uncertain site impact; persistence 40 is short-duration; velocity 80 is immediate; dependency 70 and substitutability 70 assume road/workforce reliance and scheduling flexibility, pending verification. All are provisional judgments.
components.causalPath: County-matched storm potential → possible local road or workforce access interruption → dispatch and production continuity. Actual route, utility and site effects remain unverified.
components.verify: Current county warnings, confirmed route closures, dispatch timing and site conditions. The exact Top Fox production allocation remains unknown.
components.action: Plant and logistics leaders should check the current outlook before shifts and dispatch, following existing weather procedures.
components.trigger: A warning matching an operating location, verified route closure, utility interruption or reported site impact warrants immediate reassessment and the approved continuity response.
components.dateNote: NWS issued 04:29 CDT on 17 September. Recheck within 24 hours; expiry prevents retaining this outlook as a standing condition.

observations.title: New county-matched weather outlook
observations.sourceScope: Regional NWS forecast; no observed Watershed disruption.
observations.finding: The relevant Illinois zone group covers all three known Illinois operating-presence counties. The separate southern Illinois heat-advisory zone is not attributed to these facilities.
observations.decision: Recheck local warnings and route conditions before shifts and dispatch.

observations.title: Pet-supplement ingredient recall discovery
observations.sourceScope: FDA-hosted company announcement; source publication precedes today.
observations.finding: Fi recalled dog supplements after a supplied ingredient raised potential Salmonella concerns.
observations.decision: Quality may compare applicable materials and supplier controls. A Watershed relationship or affected material is not established; do not treat this as a Watershed recall.

observations.title: Cashew-inclusion hard-material recall discovery
observations.sourceScope: Specific So Delicious frozen-dessert recall, not the whole cashew market.
observations.finding: The company reported the potential presence of stones or other hard material in cashew inclusions in one recalled frozen-dessert product.
observations.decision: Use as a foreign-material control review lead for relevant nut inclusions only. No Watershed supplier, manufacturing or customer connection is established.

observations.title: Historical company litigation notice discovered
observations.sourceScope: Administrator notice, not a current docket disposition.
observations.finding: See company-ground-truth claim F27. The notice’s scheduled approval hearing has elapsed, while the page still uses conditional language.
observations.decision: HR/legal should verify the current disposition. Do not infer liability, final approval, payment or a new incident.

observations.title: New KEV records await installed-inventory matching
observations.sourceScope: CISA catalog additions; no installed Watershed systems identified.
observations.finding: Recent vendor vulnerability records were collected successfully.
observations.decision: Authorized IT staff must match vendor, product and version before estimating company exposure. An empty company match is not a cyber clearance.

reviewNotes: Intelligence: separated retrieval dates from publication and event dates; no inferred supplier/customer links.
Operations research: scored only reviewed applicability hypotheses, kept seven unassessed domains null, and preserved the exact normalized equation.
Supply chain: fuel surcharges and truck dependence remain contract-dependent assumptions.
Industrial engineering: county outlook does not establish plant interruption, exact Top Fox production allocation or Wisconsin site exposure.
Food science/quality: sector recalls were retained as verification leads without asserting contaminated Watershed inputs or relaxing safety controls.
Information security: KEV additions require authorized inventory matching; no installed products inferred.
Continuity: outlooks are not warnings; actual applicable emergencies require approved response and explicit escalation.
limits: First dated assessment. No yesterday or 30/90/365-day backfill; older evidence is not a newly occurring event.
